authors: Ing NH, Richardson R, Lamon TK, Daigle CL

mcqs.q: After the 12-week socialization and training program, kennel-raised dogs' qualitative behavior assessment (QBA) scores:
mcqs.e: All 20 QBA behaviors improved 9-53% (p<0.006) following the interactive program.

mcqs.q: Before the program (PRE), the dogs' QBA scores showed:
o: High negative-valence and low positive-valence scores
High positive-valence and low negative-valence scores
mcqs.e: PRE scores were high for positive behaviors (Relaxed ~75) and low for negative ones (Distressed ~31).

mcqs.q: The authors concluded that regular positive human interaction for kenneled dogs primarily:
o: Increased positive valence toward humans and reduced negative responses
mcqs.e: Positive human contact was perceived to raise positive valence and lower negative responses, supporting adoptability.

authors: Yaw AM, Gardella ME, Jacobs J, Hoffmann HM

mcqs.q: Compared with standard light, which lighting condition lowered shelter cats' cortisol by day 5?
mcqs.e: Cortisol decreased under dim blue-depleted light versus standard light on day 5.

mcqs.q: An increased probability of hiding occurred only under:
mcqs.e: Hiding probability rose only in the dim, non-blue-depleted condition.

mcqs.q: Over the first days in the shelter, behavioral stress markers in cats:
mcqs.e: A behavioral approach test showed declining stress markers over time in the shelter.

authors: Barrios F, Ruiz P, Damian JP

mcqs.q: According to the review, among the most prevalent behavioral problems in domestic cats are:
mcqs.e: The review identifies fear, anxiety, and stress as among the most prevalent feline behavioral problems.

mcqs.q: To reduce stress during veterinary visits, the review recommends:
o: A cat-friendly environment plus pharmacologic management
mcqs.e: It recommends cat-friendly environmental design plus pharmacologic management for a stress-free visit.

mcqs.q: Interpreting feline behavior is complicated because cats:
o: Have emotional systems distinct from other species and humans
mcqs.e: The review notes cats' distinct emotional systems complicate interpretation of their behavior.

authors: Saengthong A, Brown JL, Towiboon P, Punturee K, Buddhasiri S, Nganvongpanit K, Punyapornwithaya V, Tocharoennirattisai W, Khonmee J

mcqs.q: Fecal glucocorticoid metabolite (fGCM) levels in disabled versus healthy long-term shelter dogs were:
mcqs.e: No significant fGCM difference was found, indicating comparable physiological stress.

mcqs.q: Compared with healthy dogs, disabled dogs showed:
o: Elevated MDA and glucose with lower triglyceride and HDL
mcqs.e: Disabled dogs had elevated MDA and glucose and lower triglyceride and HDL.

mcqs.q: The authors recommended that welfare assessment of impaired shelter dogs be:
o: Multifactorial, including metabolic and microbial parameters
mcqs.e: They advised multifactorial assessment because cortisol alone missed subclinical metabolic/microbial shifts.

authors: Chen YH, Chen CI, Lin CY, Teng KT

mcqs.q: The conditions judged most impactful on individual shelter dogs' welfare were:
o: Depressive disorders, fear/anxiety disorders, and limited space
mcqs.e: Depressive disorders, fear/anxiety disorders, and limited space had the greatest individual welfare impact.

mcqs.q: The most prevalent welfare conditions identified were:
o: Limited access to toys, insufficient foraging, and excessive barking
mcqs.e: Limited toy access, insufficient foraging, and excessive barking were the most prevalent conditions.

mcqs.q: Which Five Domains had the most significant prolonged negative welfare effects?
mcqs.e: The Physical Environment and Behavioural Interactions domains drove most welfare harm.

authors: Gunter LM, Platzer JM, Reed JL, Blade EM, Gilchrist RJ, Barber RT, Feuerbacher EN, Wynne CDL

mcqs.q: During the weeklong foster stay, shelter dogs' urinary cortisol and rest:
o: Cortisol fell and they rested more
mcqs.e: At both shelters cortisol decreased and dogs spent more time resting during fostering.

mcqs.q: On return to the shelter, dogs housed with a FAMILIAR dog:
o: Rested more and showed less high-intensity activity
mcqs.e: Co-housing with a familiar conspecific increased rest and reduced high-arousal activity on reentry.

mcqs.q: Comparing pre- versus post-fostering measures in the shelter, the authors found:
o: No significant pre/post difference except more mid-intensity activity
mcqs.e: No significant pre/post cortisol or activity difference was found, aside from more mid-intensity activity afterward.

mcqs.q: The dog quality-of-life assessment tool was grounded in:
o: The Framework of Dogs' Needs (species, breed, individual levels)
mcqs.e: The tool was built on the Framework of Dogs' Needs spanning species, breed, and individual levels.

mcqs.q: The pilot identified the main feasibility challenge as:
mcqs.e: Feasibility of participant-recorded videos was the key challenge; the time commitment was acceptable.

mcqs.q: The assessment tool comprises how many components?
mcqs.e: It has three components: participant questionnaires, investigator questionnaires with video, and participant-recorded videos.

mcqs.q: Which procedure produced the larger reduction in human-directed kennel reactivity?
mcqs.e: Response-independent treat delivery cut undesirable behavior ~88%, outperforming DRO's ~66%.

mcqs.q: In the control condition, undesirable in-kennel behavior:
mcqs.e: The control condition increased undesirable behavior by about 15%.

mcqs.q: Response-independent treat delivery was favored for shelter use because it:
o: Required less time and skill, suiting staff and volunteers
mcqs.e: It needed less time and skill, making it practical for staff and volunteers.

authors: Collins K, Miller K, Eagan BH, Patterson-Kane E, Rehner-Fleurant T, Cussen V, Reid P

mcqs.q: Dogs that began behavior modification within ~10 days of intake, versus delayed-start dogs:
mcqs.e: Early-onset behavior modification reduced fear sooner than a delayed start.

mcqs.q: A prolonged settling-in period without active treatment:
o: Did not itself improve fear-related behaviors
mcqs.e: The extended unsupported acclimation did not by itself improve fear-related behaviors.

mcqs.q: The authors concluded that, when resources allow, behavior modification should:
o: Never be used in fearful dogs
Begin as early as possible after intake
mcqs.e: Starting behavior modification early was deemed the most beneficial and ethical option.

authors: Octavio P. Luzardo, Ruth Manzanares-Fernandez, Jose Ramon Becerra-Carollo, Maria del Mar Travieso-Aja

mcqs.q: Under current (~20%) sterilization coverage, Spain's community cat population is projected to:
mcqs.e: At ~20% coverage, the model projects the population could exceed 5 million by 2050.

mcqs.q: Territory-stratified sterilization (50% in most areas, 60-70% in high-pressure zones) is projected to:
mcqs.e: The differentiated strategy stabilized the population by 2030 at about 1.5 million.

mcqs.q: The modeling implies effective free-roaming cat control requires sterilization coverage that:
o: Exceeds the replacement rate, rising with reproductive intensity
mcqs.e: Coverage must outpace reproductive output, with higher thresholds where reproductive intensity is greatest.

authors: Sheila I. Pena-Corona, Melissa Aurea Vaquera-Guerrero, Jose Cerbon-Gutierrez, Juan I. Chavez-Corona, Adrian E. Iglesias-Reyes, Alonso Sierra-Resendiz, Juan Jose Perez-Rivero, Socorro Retana-Marquez, Pablo Adrian Vizcaino-Dorado, David Quintanar-Guerrero, Gerardo Leyva-Gomez, Dinorah Vargas-Estrada

mcqs.q: The review concluded that current non-surgical contraceptives:
o: Offer permanent sterility in dogs only
Do not yet provide permanent sterility able to replace surgery
mcqs.e: No non-surgical method yet offers permanent sterility able to replace surgical spay.

mcqs.q: Regarding regulatory approval, non-surgical contraceptives for cats and dogs are:
mcqs.e: None are currently authorized by the FDA or EMA for cats or dogs.

mcqs.q: Immunocontraceptive approaches discussed target antigens including:
o: GnRH, the LH receptor, and zona pellucida proteins
mcqs.e: Immunocontraception targets GnRH, the LH receptor, zona pellucida proteins, and sperm.

authors: Lauren Margaret Smith, Tamara Kartal, Sanjay Rawat, Amit Chaudhari, Ashok Kumar, Rajesh Kumar Pandey, Rupert Julian Quinnell, Lisa M. Collins

mcqs.q: Following the CNVR program, the probability of dogs presenting with mange, transmissible venereal tumor, or pregnancy:
mcqs.e: These health/reproductive markers significantly declined over the program.

mcqs.q: Overall street counts of dogs during the study:
o: Increased overall despite more sterilized dogs
mcqs.e: Sterilized proportions rose, but overall observed dog counts increased.

mcqs.q: The findings suggest CNVR reduces population size only when coverage:
o: Is high enough to outpace recruitment and immigration
mcqs.e: Welfare improved without population reduction, so coverage must exceed recruitment/immigration to shrink numbers.
